title: compact-shell-task-tree-proposals-wip
summary: Working doc for a compact "task shell" concept: replaces persistent left rail with a task-focused collapsible shell that surfaces recent workflows, deep-links, and a hierarchical task tree. Aim: reduce vertical chrome, improve task preservation across route swaps, and simplify routing semantics for micro-apps (Models, Routes, Deployments, Jobs).
body:
Context / why this exists:
- Current left-rail is bulky for power users who do quick task switching (model -> eval -> deployment -> logs). We get repeated feedback: "I lose context when jumping between routes" and "sidebar is noisy for project-level actions".
- Goal: create a compact, keyboard-first task shell that can expand into a task tree, preserve ephemeral task state (active prompt, unsaved edits), and provide consistent deep-linking for onboarding and SRE workflows.

High-level proposal (sketch):
- Shell collapsed state (16px rail): app icon, quick-switcher hotkey (CMD+K), unread badges.
- Shell peek (hover or K): thin overlay showing 3 most recent tasks and "Create" CTA.
- Shell expanded (panel) shows: task search, pinned tasks, hierarchical task tree (Projects > Workspaces > Routes/Models > Instances), and a small context card on the right for selected task metadata (owner, last run, SLA).
- Task tree nodes are not route-level; they are task objects with metadata and last-known route/anchor. Clicking a task restores UI to the saved route and scroll/selection state if available.

Wireframe writeups (areas to hand to design):
- Compact collapsed rail: 48px tall icons, 4px vertical padding. Icons move to center when collapsed. Tooltip on hover.
- Expanded shell: fixed width 360px on desktop, 100% width on narrow screens and collapses to a bottom sheet on mobile.
- Task card layout: left: tiny favicon+title; middle: subtitle (route label + project); right: quick actions (open, pin, copy deep-link, run).
- Breadcrumb bar above main canvas when task restored: shows task lineage and a small "preserve state" toggle if the task has unsaved context.
- Mini-map: floating toggle (top-right) for dense workflows to jump between open tabs within the task: Prompts | Streams | Logs | Metrics.

Routing implications / contract:
- Introduce a canonical task URL: /t/{task_id} (task_id is stable across model/version changes). Task routes map to underlying app routes via a routing manifest.
- Service contract: task resolution must be < 200ms for perceived instant navigation; fallback to route-level redirect if task metadata stale.
- Route fallthrough: if a task references a model version not available to the user, show a read-only view + callout to suggest compatible variants.

Microflows (common user journeys):
1) "Jump to eval I was editing": cmd+k -> type 'eval heatmap' -> select task -> app restores eval editor with unsaved prompt -> user continues.
2) "Support triage": open shell, filter by 'last 24h errors', pin task -> jump to logs minimap -> open quick snapshot (stacktrace + recent tokens) -> create support ticket from shell.
3) "Deploy from task": open model task, quick action 'run deploy' -> modal shows deduped capacity suggestions (from Optimize) -> confirm -> task updated with new deployment ID and logs link.

Backlog grooming (prioritized):
- [P0] Task manifest backend (db schema + API) - 8 pts - acceptance: canonical /t/{id} resolves to correct route and includes lastKnownState payload.
- [P0] Frontend shell component + collapsed/expand behaviors - 5 pts - acceptance: keyboard nav, a11y labels, collapsed rail matches spec.
- [P1] Task restore state plumbing (scroll, form fields) - 8 pts - acceptance: preserved form edits for 3 tested flows.
- [P1] Quick actions (pin, copy link, run) + analytics - 5 pts - acceptance: events emitted, instrumentation in console.
- [P2] Mobile bottom-sheet variant - 3 pts - acceptance: responsive handoff + UX smoke test.
- [P2] RBAC checks for task visibility + compatibility modes - 5 pts - acceptance: tasks filtered server-side for non-admins.
- [P3] Mini-map + tab-switcher inside restored task - 5 pts.

Acceptance criteria (sample for P0):
- Creating a task (via UI or API) returns stable id and deep link.
- Navigating to /t/{id} should: 1) load shell state, 2) redirect main canvas to manifested route within 200ms, 3) show callout if any references are stale.
- Keyboard flow (cmd+k -> type -> enter) should be within 150ms on local dev.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should tasks be first-class persisted objects (DB) or ephemeral pointers (cache + timeline)? Persisted is simpler for deep-link durability; ephemeral reduces storage and cleanup.
- How much of state do we attempt to snapshot (entire redux state vs small curated fields)? Snapshot size impacts API latency and storage.
- Should we show disabled actions for incompatible tasks or hide them? Hiding reduces cognitive load but may confuse users who expect consistency across org.
- Performance budget: new shell should not add >2kB to base HTML payload. Consider code-splitting and lazy load.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Risk: inconsistent UX across micro-apps -> Mitigate: define shell API + small contract for micro-app teams (restore handlers).
- Risk: heavy DB growth from persisted tasks -> Mitigate: retention policy + compacted only metadata for long-term tasks.
- Risk: RBAC/visibility bugs exposing tasks -> Mitigate: server-side ACL checks and integration tests.

Instrumentation / observability notes:
- Events: task.open, task.pin, task.restore.success, task.restore.fallback, task.action.run. Include duration to restore.
- Dashboards: median restore latency, 95th percentile, task retention curve (create -> stale -> deleted).

Hand-offs / next steps (for next grooming):
- Engineering: draft task manifest proto + simple GET/POST endpoints (INF-1429).
- Design: produce hi-fi expanded shell and micro-interaction prototypes (motion timings).
- PM: draft rollout plan: opt-in per-org, telemetry gating, pilot with 3 internal teams.
- SRE: cost estimate for task metadata storage and expected QPS.

Notes to reviewers (what I want feedback on):
- Are we comfortable with a server-side persisted task model or prefer ephemeral? Pros/cons in your teams.
- UX: collapsed rail width and affordances — does 360px feel heavy? alternatives?
- Routing: is the idea of /t/{id} acceptable to infra for sticky deep links?

Sketches (textual):
- [Collapsed] |R|  (icons)  CMD+K  
- [Expanded] ------------------------------
  | Search [_____]  |  Task card list        |  Task context -> owner |
  | Pinned (3)      |  Workspaces > Routes   |  last run 2h | SLA 99.9% |
  ----------------------------------------

TL;DR: Compact task-shell trades persistent chrome for task-first navigation, improves context preservation, and simplifies deep-links for workflows. Implementation will require a small server contract and a light frontend shell; biggest unknowns are snapshot fidelity and retention policy.

decisions: Keep canonical task URL /t/{id} to simplify deep-linking and external integrations.
Persist lightweight task metadata server-side; full snapshot to be curated per flow.
Shell width set to 360px for desktop with a mobile bottom-sheet fallback.
Expose quick actions (pin, copy link, run) in list to reduce clicks.

How big of a snapshot is acceptable for restore latency?
Should we allow tasks to reference cross-project resources? (RBAC complexity)
What fallback UI should be shown when a referenced model version is missing?
